edition: The Constitution of India [As on 1st May, 2026] - Ministry of Law & Justice, Legislative Department

articles.title: Equality before law
articles.description: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
articles.relevance: Foundation of equal access to justice, non-discrimination in judicial proceedings and public administrative actions.

articles.title: Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.
articles.description: Guarantees freedom of speech and expression, peaceful assembly, forming associations/unions/co-operative societies, free movement, residence, and practice of any profession or trade.
articles.relevance: Protects trade, profession of lawyers, freedom of expression and formation of cooperative societies.

articles.title: Protection of life and personal liberty
articles.description: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.
articles.relevance: Supreme Court has interpreted right to free legal aid, speedy trial, dignity, and livelihood as integral components of Article 21.

articles.title: Right to education
articles.description: The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years (86th Amendment Act, 2002).
articles.relevance: Enforceable fundamental right for child welfare, school admission disputes, and RTE compliance.

articles.title: Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases
articles.description: Mandates that no person arrested shall be detained without being informed of grounds of arrest, and guarantees the fundamental right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of choice.
articles.relevance: Constitutional mandate for criminal bail, immediate legal representation, and magistrate production within 24 hours.

articles.title: Remedies for enforcement of Fundamental Rights (Supreme Court)
articles.description: Guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of fundamental rights via writs (Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, Certiorari).
articles.relevance: Heart and soul of the Constitution. Exercised through Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record (SCAORA) for urgent constitutional protection.

articles.title: Equal justice and free legal aid
articles.part: Part IV - Directive Principles of State Policy
articles.description: The State shall secure that the operation of the legal system promotes justice, on a basis of equal opportunity, and shall, in particular, provide free legal aid, by suitable legislation or schemes, to ensure justice is not denied by reason of economic or other disabilities (42nd Amendment Act, 1976).
articles.relevance: Direct constitutional mandate behind NyaySetu, NALSA, Tele-Law, DISHA 2.0, and Nyaya Bandhu (Pro Bono Club) scheme.

articles.title: The Union Judiciary (Supreme Court of India)
articles.description: Establishes the Supreme Court of India as a Court of Record (Art 129), its Original Jurisdiction (Art 131), Appellate Jurisdiction (Art 132-134), Special Leave to Appeal (Art 136), Binding Law (Art 141), and Inherent Powers for Complete Justice (Art 142).
articles.relevance: Regulates Supreme Court practice, Advocates-on-Record (AORs / SCAORA), and presidential references (Art 143).

articles.title: The High Courts in the States
articles.description: Establishes High Courts for States, Court of Record (Art 215), Extraordinary Writ Jurisdiction for Fundamental Rights & other legal rights (Art 226), and Power of Superintendence over all subordinate courts and tribunals (Art 227).
articles.relevance: Primary constitutional avenue for high court litigation, civil/criminal writ petitions, and district court oversight.

articles.title: Subordinate Courts (District & Sessions Judiciary)
articles.description: Provides for appointment of District Judges (Art 233), recruitment of judicial officers (Art 234), and administrative control over subordinate courts by the High Court (Art 235).
articles.relevance: Framework for District and Sessions Courts, City Civil Courts, Chief Judicial Magistrates, and trial courts across India.

articles.title: The Panchayats, Municipalities & Co-operative Societies
articles.description: Constitutionalization of local self-government institutions: Gram Sabhas & Panchayats (73rd Amendment, Art 243-243O), Municipalities & Wards (74th Amendment, Art 243P-243ZG), and Co-operative Societies (97th Amendment, Art 243ZH-243ZT).
articles.relevance: Basis for Gram Nyayalayas, village land dispute resolution, municipal planning committees, and cooperative dispute redressal.

articles.title: Right to Property
articles.description: No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law (44th Amendment Act, 1978).
articles.relevance: Constitutional human right protecting land owners, agriculturalists, and tenants against unlawful encroachment or unauthorized state acquisition.

articles.title: Administrative & Special Tribunals
articles.description: Authorizes Parliament and State Legislatures to establish Administrative Tribunals (CAT/SAT) for public employment disputes and tribunals for taxes, foreign exchange, industrial/labor disputes, land ceiling, and tenancy (42nd & 75th Amendments).
articles.relevance: Direct routing of employee grievances, service tribunal claims, consumer commissions, and labor courts.

articles.title: Reservation for Women in Parliament & State Assemblies (106th Amendment / 2026)
articles.description: Reserves one-third (33%) of all seats for women in the Lok Sabha (Art 330A), State Legislative Assemblies (Art 332A), and Delhi Assembly (Art 239AA) under the Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023 (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, effective 2026).
articles.relevance: Landmark democratic milestone for gender justice, equal political representation, and women's rights empowerment.

articles.title: Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and procedure therefor
articles.description: Specifies the constituent power and procedures for constitutional amendments by special majority and state ratifications.
articles.relevance: Governs the constitutional evolution of India across 106 Amendment Acts.

amendments.act: The Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023
amendments.title: Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (Women's Reservation in Lok Sabha & State Assemblies)
amendments.summary: Introduced Articles 330A, 332A, and 334A, reserving one-third of seats for women in Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, and National Capital Territory of Delhi Assembly.
amendments.impact: Transformational gender justice and political empowerment for women across India.

amendments.act: The Constitution (One Hundred and Fifth Amendment) Act, 2021
amendments.title: State Powers to Identify Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBCs)
amendments.summary: Amended Article 342A to clarify that States and Union Territories maintain their own authority to prepare and maintain state-specific SEBC / OBC lists.
amendments.impact: Restored state-level social justice lists and reservation administration.

amendments.act: The Constitution (One Hundred and Fourth Amendment) Act, 2019
amendments.title: Extension of SC/ST Reservations & Discontinuation of Anglo-Indian Nomination
amendments.summary: Extended reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies under Article 334 for up to 80 years (2030), while discontinuing nominated Anglo-Indian seats.
amendments.impact: Sustained affirmative action for marginalized communities.

amendments.act: The Constitution (One Hundred and Third Amendment) Act, 2019
amendments.title: 10% Reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS)
amendments.summary: Amended Articles 15(6) and 16(6) to enable up to 10% affirmative reservation in educational institutions and public employment for Economically Weaker Sections of citizens.
amendments.impact: Poverty-based affirmative action expanding access to government jobs and higher education.

amendments.act: The Constitution (One Hundred and Second Amendment) Act, 2018
amendments.title: Constitutional Status to National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC)
amendments.summary: Inserted Article 338B and Article 342A, conferring constitutional body status to NCBC on par with NCSC and NCST.
amendments.impact: Enhanced constitutional safeguards against social deprivation.

amendments.act: The Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016
amendments.title: Goods and Services Tax (GST) & GST Council
amendments.summary: Inserted Article 246A (Concurrent tax powers), Article 269A (IGST), and Article 279A (Goods and Services Tax Council).
amendments.impact: Unified national tax market and cooperative fiscal federalism.

amendments.title: Land Boundary Agreement (LBA) with Bangladesh (Appendix I)
amendments.summary: Amended First Schedule to exchange 111 Indian enclaves in Bangladesh and 51 Bangladesh enclaves in West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, and Tripura.
amendments.impact: Settled historic land disputes and provided full citizenship rights to enclave residents.

amendments.title: Right to Free and Compulsory Education (Article 21A)
amendments.summary: Inserted Article 21A making education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14, amended Article 45, and added Fundamental Duty Article 51A(k).
amendments.impact: Foundation of the Right to Education (RTE) Act.

amendments.title: Panchayati Raj Constitutionalization (Part IX & 11th Schedule)
amendments.summary: Inserted Part IX (Articles 243 to 243O) and Eleventh Schedule containing 29 subjects of rural governance and local justice.
amendments.impact: Grassroots decentralization, Gram Sabhas, and local dispute conciliation.

amendments.title: Municipalities Constitutionalization (Part IXA & 12th Schedule)
amendments.summary: Inserted Part IXA (Articles 243P to 243ZG) and Twelfth Schedule for urban local governance.
amendments.impact: Urban local self-government and municipal planning.

amendments.title: Restoration of Civil Liberties & Property as Legal Right
amendments.summary: Removed Right to Property from Fundamental Rights (Art 31) and re-enacted it under Article 300A; safeguarded Articles 20 and 21 during emergencies; substituted 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' in Article 352.
amendments.impact: Restored democracy, prevented arbitrary detention, and established robust judicial review.

amendments.title: Insertion of Article 39A (Free Legal Aid) & Fundamental Duties (Part IVA)
amendments.summary: Inserted Article 39A (Equal justice and free legal aid), Part IVA (Article 51A Fundamental Duties), Part XIVA (Tribunals), and added 'Socialist Secular' to the Preamble.
amendments.impact: Created the legal constitutional basis for NALSA, Tele-Law, and state free legal aid clinics.

amendments.title: Land Reforms, Saving of Estates (Art 31A/31B) & Ninth Schedule
amendments.summary: Inserted Articles 31A, 31B, the Ninth Schedule, and reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2).
amendments.impact: Protected agrarian land reform laws against constitutional challenges.
